headline: Rates remain the dominant driver (10Y ~5.3%, highest since 2002), equities near records; Hyperliquid data is back and shows crypto softening, ETH weakest of the majors
tldr: Hyperliquid's API was reachable this run, so crypto levels are now measured: BTC ~$82.5K (-1.5% 24h), ETH ~$2,538 (-1.5% 24h, about 7% below the Oct 5 print in the prior brief), total perp OI ~$12.4B across 178 listed markets. Macro and equities are unchanged from the 06:00 run: Fed funds 3.75-4.00% after the Sep 16 hike, 10Y ~5.27-5.34%, S&P 500 7,773.95 at the Oct 5 close (no Oct 6-7 close found). Oil was reported near $107 in late September amid a US-Iran conflict (stale, low-confidence). Watch: Oct 18 Russia/Iran sanctions deadline, September CPI, Oct 27-28 FOMC. Not financial advice.

domains.summary: Policy is tightening: the FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 (first hike since 2023) and 16 of 18 participants projected at least one more hike this year. Long yields spiked on Oct 5 (10Y about 5.34%, 30Y about 5.70%, highest since 2002) and eased slightly on Oct 6 (10Y about 5.27%). We read the liquidity backdrop as tightening. No September CPI print or current oil/dollar levels could be verified this run.

US cash market status at write time unknown; levels are as of the Oct 5-6 sessions. Indexes are near record highs despite the rates spike, with AI-linked names accounting for the bulk of 2026 index gains per Jefferies. Volatility was subdued at the last verified reading (VIX 15.31 on Oct 2). No put/call or Oct 7 close found.

Hyperliquid metaAndAssetCtxs fetched live this run. Perp OI totals about $12.4B (BTC ~$3.29B, ETH ~$2.97B, HYPE ~$1.70B, SOL ~$0.65B, ZEC ~$0.57B); this is below the ~$18B platform OI record cited for Sep 23 (the two figures may be computed differently, so we treat the gap as low-confidence). Funding sits at the 0.00125%/h baseline on BTC and most alts while ETH is slightly negative (-0.0002%/h), so ETH is the one major where shorts are paying less than longs elsewhere; we read that as mild relative weakness. 24h moves are red across the majors (BTC -1.5%, ETH -1.5%, SOL -3.1%, HYPE -3.6%, XRP -3.2%). Spot BTC reports of ~$84-87K from Oct 2 are stale versus the $82.5K HL mark. Spot ETF flows were small and positive for BTC early October, ETH ETFs saw outflows. Fear & Greed, DVOL and stablecoin cap were not retrieved.

Individual mega-cap quotes for Oct 6-7 could not be found this run, so dispersion is not assessed. Context: AI-linked stocks drove more than 80% of S&P 500 gains in 2026 per Jefferies, hyperscaler 2026 capex estimates run $520-725B depending on scope, and NVDA is about 22% of SMH, keeping semis breadth concentrated. Oct 2 coverage described semis as split.

The Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (signed Sep 18) requires implementation within 30 days (Oct 18), with authority for tariffs up to 100% on top importers of Russian energy, subject to waivers. Separately reported: US-Canada 50% tariffs after talks broke down (undated roundup), prospective new China overcapacity tariffs, new Iran-related Treasury sanctions, and an Iran-Oman Hormuz transit framework. Current Brent/WTI and OPEC+ news not found.

thesis.observe: The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16. The 10Y was about 5.31% at the Oct 5 close (5.34% intraday high, 5.27% on Oct 6). The S&P 500 closed at 7,773.95 on Oct 5. On Hyperliquid, BTC is $82,493 (-1.5% 24h), ETH $2,538 (-1.5%), SOL $113.64 (-3.1%), HYPE $86.01 (-3.6%); perp OI totals about $12.4B; ETH funding is slightly negative while BTC funding sits at baseline. A Russia/Iran sanctions law has an Oct 18 deadline. September CPI, Oct 6-7 closes, oil, gold and mega-cap quotes were not retrievable.
thesis.infer: Crypto appears to be softening ahead of, rather than alongside, the equity market, which is still near records; we read that as crypto being more sensitive to the 10Y at ~5.3% than AI-led equities are. Consensus is pricing roughly even odds of an October hike; the missing September CPI limits how far we diverge. Lower measured OI than the Sep 23 record is consistent with de-risking, but the metric difference makes this low-confidence.
thesis.forecast: Base case (we lean here, low-confidence): range-bound-to-soft crypto while long yields stay elevated, with equities near highs. Tail case (low-confidence): a further long-end yield spike or hot CPI forces a repricing of hike odds, and risk skews toward a sharper leg down in high-beta alts and long-duration tech. Second tail case (low-confidence): tariff implementation under the Oct 18 sanctions deadline broadens into a trade shock. Consensus is pricing a split decision in October; we read the risk as hinging on September CPI.
thesis.disclaimer: Not financial advice. Market intelligence only — a reasoned read of public data, not a recommendation to buy or sell anything.

risks: Further long-end yield spike (30Y already above 5.7%) pressuring valuations
Hawkish surprise at the Oct 27-28 FOMC or hot September CPI
Tariff escalation tied to the Oct 18 Russia/Iran sanctions deadline or US-Canada/China trade measures
Data-quality risk: equity, oil, gold and mega-cap levels are from Oct 5 or earlier; only Hyperliquid data is live this run
